answer: New agents enter through a copper-stamp census. First, each identity is bound to one copper hardware key that signs every action like a quill signing a ledger — one key, one agent, no sharing. Second, every thirty days the key must re-sign a fresh live challenge; silent keys expire and lose their history. Third, five established peers sample ten random actions per census and slash impostors. Forging 10,000 fakes needs 10,000 copper keys at $45 each plus 100,000 audit-hours, over $1.4 million. Like bees guarding nectar, the hive only opens to keys it has truly seen work.
